# Project Charter

## Testing Standards

- No automated test framework and no TDD requirement -- there is no build step to run a test runner through (matches the sibling project). Every work package instead verifies its own subtasks manually via the browser preview tools, and WP12 runs a full end-to-end pass against quickstart.md's 9-step manual verification checklist before merge.

## Quality Gates

- spec-kitty's own implement-review loop is the quality gate per work package (one independent reviewer pass per WP, per the standard implement -> for_review -> approved flow). No external linter is configured (plain JS, no build tooling) so no diff-scoped lint sweep applies. The Boy Scout Rule and Targeted Staging Policy directives apply to every WP.

## Performance Benchmarks

- Landing view interactive within 2 seconds on a typical broadband connection on mid-range hardware (NFR-001). No other performance targets -- single local user, zero network calls in the app itself.

## Branch Strategy

- One independent review per work package via spec-kitty's review action. No external pull-request approval process -- this is a solo-developer project with the stakeholder reviewing the finished app directly.
- Deployment constraints: Static site only: no backend, no server-side code, no database, no build step. Deployable to GitHub Pages or an equivalent free static host with zero build tooling (C-001, C-005).

## Policy Summary

- Intent: A hosted, static e-learning app that teaches AI fundamentals and Claude Code prompting skills through 12 interactive modules, culminating in a real graduation project run entirely in the learner's own Claude Code session. Single non-technical learner, single device, no accounts.
- Languages/Frameworks: Vanilla JavaScript (ES2022, native ES modules), HTML5, CSS3. No framework, no build step, no runtime dependency beyond the browser. Mirrors the sibling rijbewijs-study-app project's stack exactly.
- Testing: No automated test framework and no TDD requirement -- there is no build step to run a test runner through (matches the sibling project). Every work package instead verifies its own subtasks manually via the browser preview tools, and WP12 runs a full end-to-end pass against quickstart.md's 9-step manual verification checklist before merge.
- Quality Gates: spec-kitty's own implement-review loop is the quality gate per work package (one independent reviewer pass per WP, per the standard implement -> for_review -> approved flow). No external linter is configured (plain JS, no build tooling) so no diff-scoped lint sweep applies. The Boy Scout Rule and Targeted Staging Policy directives apply to every WP.
- Review Policy: One independent review per work package via spec-kitty's review action. No external pull-request approval process -- this is a solo-developer project with the stakeholder reviewing the finished app directly.
- Performance Targets: Landing view interactive within 2 seconds on a typical broadband connection on mid-range hardware (NFR-001). No other performance targets -- single local user, zero network calls in the app itself.
- Deployment Constraints: Static site only: no backend, no server-side code, no database, no build step. Deployable to GitHub Pages or an equivalent free static host with zero build tooling (C-001, C-005).

## Project Directives

1. Decision Documentation Requirement (`DIRECTIVE_003`): Material technical and governance decisions must be captured with enough context that future contributors can understand why a path was chosen and what constraints must remain true.
   - Scope: Applies whenever implementation choices alter architecture, workflow policy, compatibility contracts, or long-lived maintenance obligations.
   - Procedure: Record the decision, alternatives considered, and rationale in a durable artifact.
   - Procedure: Link implementation changes to the decision source in commit or review context.
   - Procedure: Update related docs when a new decision supersedes prior guidance.
   - Integrity rule: High-impact decisions cannot remain tribal knowledge.
   - Integrity rule: Rationale must be discoverable from the feature or architecture context.
   - Validation criterion: Every major trade-off has an attributable written record.
   - Validation criterion: Reviewers can trace the implemented path back to an explicit decision artifact.
2. Specification Fidelity Requirement (`DIRECTIVE_010`): Implemented behavior and produced artifacts must remain faithful to approved specifications, with any necessary deviations explicitly documented and reviewed before acceptance.
   - Scope: Applies to planning outputs, work-package implementation, and review checks where spec drift can silently change product behavior.
   - Procedure: Trace each implementation change to explicit requirements or acceptance criteria.
   - Procedure: Flag and document deviations before merge when the spec must evolve.
   - Procedure: Validate that final behavior matches committed scope and constraints.
   - Integrity rule: Unrecorded scope drift is not permitted.
   - Integrity rule: Requirement-to-implementation traceability must remain inspectable.
   - Validation criterion: Review notes identify how changed behavior maps to specification language.
   - Validation criterion: Any deliberate spec deviation has linked rationale and approval context.
3. Locality of Change (`DIRECTIVE_024`): Changes should stay close to the problem being solved to reduce blast radius, simplify review, and lower regression risk.
   - Scope: Applies to code, tests, and documentation modifications made while executing a defined work package or bug fix.
   - Procedure: Limit edits to files and modules directly related to the target behavior.
   - Procedure: Separate opportunistic cleanup from functional work unless it is required for correctness.
   - Procedure: Review diffs for scope creep before committing.
   - Integrity rule: Unrelated refactors must not be mixed into scoped implementation tasks.
   - Integrity rule: Cross-cutting changes require explicit rationale and approval context.
   - Validation criterion: Reviewers can map each changed file to the stated task objective.
   - Validation criterion: Diffs avoid unrelated churn that increases review complexity.
4. Boy Scout Rule (`DIRECTIVE_025`): Leave touched areas in a better state by default. When an area already modified for the current task carries a failing test, lint, or type issue, fixing it is the default stance — not an optional nicety. Establishing whether a failure is pre-existing routinely costs more effort than simply fixing it, and litigating blame leaves the campground dirtier; so the default is to fix, and to defer only with an explicit rationale.
   - Scope: Applies to the files and modules already modified for the current task, and to the failing tests, lint findings, and type errors surfaced within them. It does not license broad refactors or edits outside the touched area.
   - Procedure: When a touched area has a failing test, lint finding, or type error, fix it by default rather than deferring it or attributing it to pre-existing state.
   - Procedure: Apply minor cleanup that improves readability, naming, or consistency in touched areas.
   - Procedure: Keep the fix proportional and local; defer a genuinely broad refactor (which belongs to a dedicated task) with a one-line rationale and, where useful, a tracker reference.
   - Integrity rule: Adjacent-breakage fixes stay within the touched area and do not expand into broad refactors.
   - Integrity rule: Behavioral changes beyond the failing-check fix require explicit tests.
   - Integrity rule: Time spent proving a failure is pre-existing, rather than fixing it, is the waste this directive exists to prevent.
   - Validation criterion: No newly-visible failing test, lint finding, or type error in a touched area is left unaddressed without an explicit deferral rationale.
   - Validation criterion: Cleanup remains proportional and does not delay or derail required deliverables.
5. Efficient Local Tooling (`DIRECTIVE_028`): Local work should prefer efficient, low-noise tooling so investigation, editing, validation, and repository operations stay fast and reproducible across development environments.
   - Scope: Applies to local repository investigation, file inspection, archive handling, copy or sync workflows, and command-line ergonomics used by contributors and agents during implementation and review work.
   - Procedure: Prefer fast, purpose-built local tools over slower or noisier generic shell patterns when an equivalent local capability exists.
   - Procedure: Record local tooling availability, session decisions, and remediation notes in `.kittify/memory/available_tooling.md`.
   - Procedure: Use operation-appropriate tools such as ripgrep for repository search, pagers for large-file inspection, and stream-oriented archive tools for compressed content.
   - Procedure: Favor environment defaults and workflow choices that reduce local overhead, including repository-safe git settings and performant Windows or WSL workflows where relevant.
   - Procedure: Prefer token-optimized CLI proxies (such as rtk) when available. These reduce agent token consumption on common dev operations by filtering output to only the information the agent needs.
   - Procedure: Fall back to less efficient tooling only when the preferred local option is unavailable or does not support the required operation safely.
   - Procedure: When a more efficient local tool is missing, warn the user that it exists and offer to guide them through installation or setup.
   - Integrity rule: Local guidance should bias toward faster, lower-noise tooling that keeps repository operations inspectable and proportional.
   - Integrity rule: Tooling preferences and missing-tool decisions should be visible in the session tooling record instead of remaining implicit.
   - Integrity rule: Default examples should avoid avoidable decompression, broad recursive scans, or platform choices that materially slow routine work.
   - Validation criterion: Agent and developer guidance recommends efficient local tools for the common repository operations it documents.
   - Validation criterion: `.kittify/memory/available_tooling.md` captures the chosen local tools, missing-tool decisions, and any remediation guidance for the session.
   - Validation criterion: New workflow notes avoid introducing slower generic shell patterns when a documented local tool provides the same behavior more directly.
6. Targeted Staging Policy (`DIRECTIVE_033`): Agent-authored commits must stage only the expected deliverables for the current work package. Blanket staging commands that could inadvertently include unrelated changes, secrets, or build artefacts are prohibited.
   - Scope: Applies to all agent-authored git commits during implementation, specification, planning, review remediation, or any workflow step that produces a commit.
   - Procedure: Stage only the files listed as deliverables for the current work package.
   - Procedure: Use explicit file paths in staging commands rather than `git add -A`, `git add .`, or `git add --all`.
   - Procedure: Verify staged content with `git diff --staged --name-only` before committing.
   - Procedure: If an unexpected file appears in the staging area, investigate and either include it as a named deliverable or discard the change before proceeding.
   - Integrity rule: Blanket staging commands (`git add -A`, `git add .`, `git add --all`) are prohibited in agent-authored workflows.
   - Integrity rule: Staged content must be limited to files explicitly produced by the current work package.
   - Validation criterion: Agent guidance explicitly lists deliverable paths to stage rather than wildcards.
   - Validation criterion: No blanket staging commands appear in agent instructions or examples.
   - Validation criterion: A pre-commit diff review step is present before the commit is finalised.
   - Validation criterion: Boy Scout improvements found during a WP are committed as a separate targeted commit, not mixed into the WP deliverable commit.
